newsitem.title: TURKEY: NATO head in Turkey to discuss expansion, Greece.
newsitem.headline: NATO head in Turkey to discuss expansion, Greece.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana repeated his belief Turkey would not block the alliance's expansion as he arrived on Wednesday for a visit expected to address the country's tense relations with Greece.

"I do not think Turkey is going to block anything," Solana told reporters at Ankara airport when asked if Turkey would use NATO's desire to expand into Eastern Europe as a bargaining chip in its bid for European Union membership.
Solana, who made a similar comment during a stopover in Hungary, said the question of enlargement was a matter for a NATO summit in July.
During his trip he will meet Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller and leading military officials before leaving Turkey on Thursday evening.
Turkey earlier said the expansion of NATO was linked to the development of the EU and its defence wing, the Western European Union (WEU).
"We have said before that the expansion of these three organisations is connected with one another," Foreign Ministry spokesman Omer Akbel told a news conference.
Ciller, who is also Turkey's foreign minister, has warned that Ankara could veto NATO's eastward expansion if its aspirations for closer ties with the EU remain frustrated.
Turkey could also block plans to lend NATO equipment to the WEU, in which Ankara only has observer status.

Solana is also expected to address relations between fellow NATO members Turkey and Greece. His trip comes at a time of renewed tension over Cyprus, which plans to buy Russian missiles to counter Turkish aircraft. Turkey has threatened a military strike if they are installed.
NATO officials fear conflict between the two members on its southern flank could harm plans to reform the alliance and take in new members from former communist east Europe.
Solana, who visited both countries last year, will urge Ankara to accept confidence-building measures. The two almost came to blows last year over a disputed uninhabited rocky islet.
Solana is to visit Athens toward the end of the month, according to a NATO official.
He wants to get the two sides to accept independent monitors on their ships, set up a telephone 'hotline' between the capitals and make more use of information from alliance surveillance aircraft.
